newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end lower after confirming 124.30 ceiling.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end lower after confirming 124.30 ceiling.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended lower on Wednesday after the contract confirmed resistance at around 124.30.
"The market paused after rising mainly on short-covering for the past several days," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.

Selling was seen at the long-end of the JGB yield curve, traders said. Sentiment was also hurt by falls in bank debentures after a domestic newspaper report said the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau had not bought bank debentures since April, they said.
But the September ended off its session low of 123.80.

"There was no change in the market's view of the economy or (Japanese) interest rates. The market was moving to and fro before the Bank of Japan's tankan survey (due on June 25)," said a dealer at another city bank's securities unit.
The September closed at 123.99, down 0.31 from the previous close. Turnover was 42,010 contracts.

Earlier in the morning, the contract rose as high as 124.31, close to Tuesday's session high of 124.34, but it failed to rise further due to large-lot selling toward the end of the morning session, traders said.
